(per Hon'ble Sri Justice Laxmi Narayana Alishetty) Heard learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant and Sri M.Venkata Narayana Reddy, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

2. This appeal, under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, (for short 'the Act') is filed by the Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition), Shamshabad Mandal, Ranga Reddy District, aggrieved by the order and decree dated 18.02.2013 passed in L.A.O.P.No.158 of 2006 on the file of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B. Nagar, Hyderabad (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Court').
3.

entities.text: I Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case are that on requisition sent by the Zonal Manager, A.P. Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Limited, for acquisition of lands situated at Imamguda Village for laying approach road to the Hardware park, land to an extent of Ac.0.19 guntas in Sy.No.19 of Imamguda Village, Maheshwaram Mandal, 2 AKS,J & LNA, J belonging to the respondents/claimants was acquired; that under urgency clause, the draft notification under Section 4(1) and the draft declaration under Section 6 of the Act were approved by the District Collector, Ranga Reddy District and were effected on 29.04.2005 and 30.04.2005, respectively; and that the Land Acquisition Officer, after conducting necessary award enquiry, passed Award, dated 08.08.2005, fixing market value of the acquired land @ Rs.80,000/- per acre.
4.

The respondents/claimants received the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer under protest and sought reference under Section 18 of the Act and the same was numbered as L.A.O.P.No.158 of 2006 on the file of the Reference Court.
5. Before the Reference Court, on behalf of the respondents/claimants, P.Ws.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A-1 to A-7 were marked.
On behalf of the Referring Officer, R.W-1 was examined and Ex.B-1 was marked.

6. The Reference Court by the impugned order enhanced the market value of the acquired land to Rs.6,30,000/- per acre from 3 AKS,J & LNA, J Rs.80,000/- per acre, apart from granting other The Special Deputy Collector L.A vs K.Balakistaiah And 3 Others on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185538978/
1 benefits under the Act to the respondents/ claimants.

sentences.text: 7. Aggrieved by the impugned order passed by the Reference Court, the present appeal is filed.

8. Learned Government Pleader for Appeals appearing for the appellant-Land Acquisition Officer contended that the Reference Court erred in relying upon Ex.A-5, which relates to sale of the land abutting Hyderabad-Srisailam Highway and taking it as comparable sale, whereas the acquired land is far away from the said Highway; that the Reference Court erred in not appreciating the oral and documentary evidence from a proper perspective; and thus, the Reference Court erred in enhancing the market value of the acquired lands exorbitantly and therefore, the impugned order is liable to be set aside.

9. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants contended that the acquired lands are nearer to Srisailam-Hyderabad State Highway and taking the same into account, the Reference Court has considered Ex.A-5 as comparable sale and rightly enhanced the market value of the acquired lands 4 AKS,J & LNA, J and as such, this Appeal is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
10.
Before the Reference Court, to substantiate their claim for enhancement of compensation, the respondents/claimants have got marked Exs.A-1 to A-7.
Ex .A-1 is the valuation certificate for the year 2006.

In view of the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Choda Dharampal Reddy Vs.
Revenue Divisional Officer, Nalgonda District 1, that the valuation certificate issued by the Sub- Registrar, on the basis of the Basic Valuation Register, was only relevant for the purpose of the Stamp Act and that, such a valuation certificate cannot form basis for determination of the market value under Section 23 of the Act, therefore, Ex.A-1 cannot be considered for determination of market value of the acquired land.

11. Exs.A-3 and A-4 are the sale deeds, dated 02.01.2008 and 22.02.2008, respectively, i.e., they pertain to post-notification and hence, the same cannot be taken as exemplar sale deeds and are,
accordingly, discarded.
1998(1) ALD 261 (DB) 5 AKS,J & LNA, J 12.

Ex .A-5 is the registered sale deed, dated 26.09.2004, whereunder the land in Sy.No.3 of Imamguda Village was sold @ Rs.6,30,000/- per acre.
13.

Exs.A-6 and A-7 are the registered sale deed, dated 18.11.2006 and registered agreement of sale-cum-GPA, dated 16.10.2006, respectively, in respect of land in Sy.Nos.19, 20 and 21,
whereunder the claimants are the vendors.

It is to be noted that the said sale deeds were executed post-notification, therefore, the possibility of the claimants mentioning higher sale transaction thereunder for the purpose of buttressing their claim for enhancement of market value of the acquired lands cannot be ruled out, and as such, credence cannot be given to Exs.A-6 and A-7.

sentences.text: Now, the evidence that remains on record is Ex.A-5-sale deed, dated 26.09.2004, which was executed in respect of land in Sy.No.3 of Imamguda Village, as stated supra.
The said land is said to be abutting Srisailam-Hyderabad Highway, which remained undisputed by the Land Acquisition Officer.

The evidence of P.W-1 that the distance between the subject acquired land and 6 AKS,J &
LNA, J Srisailam Highway is 150 to 200 yards remained unrebutted by the Land Acquisition Officer.

15. It is pertinent to note that while considering the sale statistics for determination of market value of the acquired land, in Ex.B-1-Award, the Land Acquisition Officer has referred to and verified the sale statistics pertaining to Ex.A-5-sale deed, however, discarded the same on the ground that the land covered thereunder is abutting Srisailam-Hyderabad State Highway, well developed and with structures raised therein, whereas the acquired land is far away from Srisailam-Hyderabad Highway and therefore, Ex.A-5 cannot be considered for fixing the market value of the acquired land.

This observation of the Land Acquisition Officer in Ex.B-1- Award cannot be sustained for the reason that while determining the market value of the acquired land, he has also collected the sales statistics pertaining to Ex.A-5-sale deed, which pertains to land in Sy.No.3 and has not denied the statement of P.W-1 that the subject acquired land is situated at a distance of 150 to 200 yards from Srisailam Highway.
Further, it is to be noted that in Ex.B-1- Award, at page-6 at Sl.No.18, the Land Acquisition Officer verified the sale statistics pertaining to land in Sy.No.3.

This aspect 7 AKS,J &
LNA, J of Ex.B-1-Award coupled with his non-denial of statement of P.W-1 regarding the location of the acquired land, goes to show that if the acquired land in Sy.No.19 is not in the vicinity of Sy.No.3,
the Land Acquisition Officer would not have taken the sale statistics pertaining to Ex.A-5,
whereunder the land in Sy.No.3 was sold @ Rs.6,30,000/- per acre.
This undoubtedly gives a presumption that the subject acquired land in Sy.No.19 has the same potentiality as that of land in Sy.No.3.

Moreover, as mentioned supra, the evidence of P.W-1 about the location of the subject acquired land i.e., location of acquired land at a distance of 150 to 200 yards from the Srisailam road, was not denied by the Land Acquisition Officer, as observed by the Reference Court in the impugned order.

Therefore, this Court is of the considered view that the Reference Court has rightly assessed the market value of the subject acquired land by taking Ex.A-5 as exemplar sale deed and fixed the market value @ Rs.6,30,000/- per acre, which is just and reasonable.
16.
Therefore, in view of the above, this Court finds no illegality or irregularity in the impugned order of the Reference Court warranting interference by this Court.
8 AKS,J & LNA, J 17.
Accordingly, this Appeal is dismissed.
18. As a sequel, interim order, dated 12.11.2014, shall stand vacated.
Miscellaneous Petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.
